name: WC Korkmaz Contract – Contracts for WooCommerce
author: yemlihakorkmaz

sections.description:
This plugin lets you create distance sales contracts, pre-information forms, and fully custom legal contracts for WooCommerce. It automatically fills the contracts at checkout and emails them as PDF attachments after order confirmation.

  • Fully compatible with WooCommerce’s new block-based checkout.
  • Add and edit legal contracts from the WordPress admin.
  • Choose a PDF design for each contract and adjust section order, logo, typography, colors and page margins with an actual PDF preview.
  • Insert any order/customer/store data into any part of your contract via placeholders.
  • Automatically generate contracts on the checkout page.
  • Automatically send contracts in PDF format upon order confirmation.
  • View past contracts on both admin and customer order pages.
  • Store emailed PDFs under the WordPress uploads directory and serve customer downloads through protected links.

Localization

This plugin is translation-ready. Source strings are in en_US (English – United States). Complete bundled interface catalogs are provided for Turkish (tr_TR), German (de_DE), French (fr_FR), Spanish (es_ES) and Arabic (ar), including WooCommerce Blocks JavaScript translations. Existing WordPress and Loco Translate catalogs retain priority. Saved contract texts, custom labels and company information remain administrator content; changing the interface language does not automatically translate them.
Contribute translations here:
https://translate.wordpress.org/projects/wp-plugins/wc-korkmaz-contract/

Arabic interface translation and RTL controls are included. Dompdf has limitations with complex-script shaping and bidirectional text, so Arabic contract PDF typography is not guaranteed by the interface translation. Check the actual PDF preview before using an Arabic contract. Background: https://github.com/dompdf/dompdf/issues/3091

External Services

  • yemlihakorkmaz.com/sozlesmeornek.txt — used to fetch the default contract template.
    Data sent: none (HTTP GET). Privacy: https://yemlihakorkmaz.com/privacy

This external request is used only when contract templates are empty and the plugin needs a sample template.

Development and third-party libraries

PDF previews use Mozilla PDF.js 6.4.299, distributed locally under Apache-2.0 (build/pdfjs-LICENSE.txt). The viewer and worker load only when an administrator opens a PDF preview; no external viewer service or CDN is used. Source: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/ — API examples: https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

To rebuild the JavaScript assets, use Node.js 22.13 or newer, run npm ci and npm run build in the source directory. Node.js and node_modules are not needed on the WordPress server.

To refresh translation catalogs after changing interface text, run sh scripts/build-translations.sh with WP-CLI i18n and GNU gettext installed. The source-to-bundle mapping generates JSON catalogs for the actual registered checkout and editor script paths. Fill newly added PO entries before release.
sections.installation:
1. Download the plugin here or install it from Plugins → Add New in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. (Manual) Upload and extract the archive into /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Go to Plugins → Installed Plugins and click Activate.
  4. A new Contracts menu will appear in the admin — add your contracts there.
  5. On a fresh installation, complete Contracts → Setup Wizard. Until completion, administrator screens return to the wizard; plugin management and required background/media services remain available. Existing installations keep their settings and can launch the wizard manually.
sections.faq:
Is it completely free to use?

Yes. The plugin is completely free to use. No charges apply.

What does the setup wizard require?

The five steps check WooCommerce, collect company details and contract names, save the two contract texts with optional PDF designs, and ask for a final review. Empty contract texts and missing required company fields cannot advance. Progress is saved between visits; future steps cannot be opened directly. Completing setup restores normal administrator navigation. Contract acceptance stays required at checkout.

On a fresh installation the wizard is mandatory for users who can manage plugin settings. Plugin installation/activation, login/logout, media requests, AJAX, REST, cron and CLI continue to work. Network administration is excluded. Existing installations are not forced through setup after an update. “Run setup again” preserves saved texts and designs and starts the mandatory flow explicitly.

I don’t want PDFs to be sent via email. Can I disable this?

Yes. There is a setting on the plugin’s settings page to disable PDF email attachments.

When are contract PDFs prepared?

The accepted contract text is saved with the order immediately. PDFs are generated in the background through WooCommerce Action Scheduler (with WP-Cron as a fallback), so rendering does not delay payment. The queue needs working WordPress cron or a server cron runner. While files are pending, the order page shows a preparation notice and protected download links. Notifications configured to include contract PDFs wait for the files; temporary failures are retried. A shop manager can use the order action “Retry contract PDF generation” after fixing a persistent failure.

How do I change a contract’s PDF appearance?

Open the contract editor and expand “PDF design”. Choose Simple, Corporate or Minimal, then adjust the heading, local PNG/JPEG logo, company details, text, closing note, section order, fonts, colors, A4 orientation and margins. Use “Preview PDF” before saving. “Current appearance (unchanged)” preserves the existing layout. Design settings are saved separately for each contract and captured with new orders; later edits do not change an existing order’s saved design. Existing PDFs are retained. Closing notes appear in the PDF only; contract terms belong in the main contract text.

The preview uses sample data and the same Dompdf renderer as order PDFs, without creating an order or storing a preview PDF. Remote images and third-party shortcodes are excluded from previews. The local logo must remain available until background PDF generation finishes.

How are stored contract PDFs protected on Apache and Nginx?

The plugin writes an Apache .htaccess rule into the contract PDF folder and serves customer/admin downloads through protected WordPress URLs. Nginx does not read .htaccess, so the settings screen includes a direct-access security check and a copyable Nginx location rule for your server block.

How can I disable the ID/Tax number fields?

Use the option on the plugin’s settings page to hide or disable those fields.

I need more support. What should I do?

Please email: yemlihakorkmaz@hotmail.com
sections.changelog:
2.5.2

  • Admin: Apply the setup wizard’s colors and panel layout to contract editors, settings and advanced field mappings. Clarify visibility controls, show explicit enabled/disabled states and explain the effect of disabling checkout approval.
  • Orders: Replace plain document links with accessible, colored PDF cards in admin order details, both HPOS and legacy order lists, customer order details and the thank-you page. Display preparation and availability states while preserving protected download URLs.
  • Email: Add HTML and plain-text summaries for available contract PDF attachments. Clarify notification timing and the lack of an automatic pending-payment notification; preserve background generation, deferred notifications and retries.
  • Translation: Refresh all five bundled interface catalogs, including mobile and RTL presentation. Preserve saved settings, contract text, PDF designs and checkout acceptance validation.

2.5.1

  • Admin: Redesign the setup wizard with a progress sidebar, compact mobile steps, grouped company/contract/email fields, review cards and a clearer completion screen. Preserve setup validation, saved data and all bundled interface languages.

2.5.0

  • Translation: Bundle complete German, French, Spanish and Arabic interface catalogs, refresh all PHP/Blocks translation files, preserve custom catalogs and improve RTL interface alignment.
  • Setup: Add a five-step Setup Wizard under Contracts, mandatory on fresh installations, with saved progress, validated company/contract settings, existing PDF previews, server-side step checks and final review. Gate administrator navigation until completion while keeping plugin management and background services available; preserve existing installations and allow an explicit rerun.
  • PDF design: Add independent Simple, Corporate and Minimal presets for each contract, configurable sections, local logos, typography, colors, A4 orientation, margins and page numbering. Keep the existing appearance as the default and freeze the selected design with each new order.
  • Admin: Preview the actual Dompdf output before saving, with a locally bundled, lazily loaded PDF.js viewer, page navigation, readable page text and a download option. Keep PDF rendering out of the checkout request.
  • Admin: Add contract-specific titles, preparation steps, a variable picker shared by Visual/Code views, an insertable starter outline and an unsaved sample-data preview. Preview requires administrator permission and a nonce, runs in a sandbox and creates no orders or PDFs.
  • Admin: Prevent accidental loss of unsaved edits, show save results, reject empty templates and require correction or explicit acknowledgement of unknown placeholders. Keep existing template data and registered shortcode support.
  • Admin: Group advanced field mappings, keep save actions visible, synchronize custom selectors, name all field pickers for assistive technology and collapse technical server details.
  • Performance: Save accepted contract text during checkout and generate PDFs through Action Scheduler in the background, with locks, bounded retries, protected downloads and an authorized order retry action. Preserve configured PDF email attachments by deferring the relevant notifications until documents are ready.
  • Performance: Use WordPress entity decoding, memoize contract rendering, ignore unrelated input events and avoid loading classic checkout scripts/styles on block-only checkout pages.
  • Accessibility: Make contract reading links keyboard accessible, preserve explicit checkbox acceptance, and improve the contract dialog on small screens.
  • Translation: Fill missing PHP translations from the bundled catalog while preserving existing WordPress and Loco translations, including locale changes.

2.4.13

  • Fix: Load the Legal Contracts stylesheet through block metadata and keep 24px of vertical spacing around the contract area, independently of theme block gaps. Verify block and classic checkout on Twenty Twenty-Five, Twenty Twenty-Four, Storefront and Astra at desktop and mobile widths.
  • Fix: Mark the unaccepted contract checkbox as invalid through WooCommerce’s CheckboxControl API so checkout focuses it instead of falling back to the top of the page. Preserve the first invalid field priority and associate the validation message with the checkbox for assistive technologies.
  • Security: Update Dompdf to 3.1.6 and refresh its font, SVG, HTML and CSS dependencies. Verify Turkish contract PDFs, images, multi-page tables and email attachments on a separate local WordPress/WooCommerce installation.

2.4.12

  • Fix: Keep the Legal Contracts block at its saved checkout position, including older self-closing blocks, and preserve the merchant’s editor layout.
  • Fix: Load WordPress JavaScript translations from normalized script URLs and preserve custom Loco Translate catalogs.
  • Fix: Register the correct WooCommerce data store script dependency and support legacy empty contract blocks in the editor.
  • Compatibility: Verified with WordPress 7.1.3 and WooCommerce 11.2.1, including classic and block checkout approval, local bank transfer orders, and contract PDF downloads.

2.4.11

  • Admin: Show missing checkout field notices only on the plugin’s own admin pages.

2.4.10

  • Admin: Limit missing checkout field notices to the main WordPress dashboard screen only.

2.4.9

  • Fix: Center contract modals on narrow mobile screens, including iOS Safari, instead of letting the dialog align to the left edge.

2.4.8

  • Fix: Delay block type metadata registration until WordPress has initialized translations, avoiding WordPress 7.0 early textdomain notices in admin and update screens.

2.4.7

  • Fix: Avoid early translation calls from plugin action links, activation defaults, and block script data before WordPress initializes translations.

2.4.6

  • Fix: Moved block checkout additional field registration to a later WooCommerce hook to avoid early translation loading notices.
  • Fix: Plugin translations and upgrade routines now run from init with explicit priorities.

2.4.5

  • Fix: Classic checkout contract previews now read the selected option from mapped select field wrappers, preventing full state/country option lists from appearing in contract text.

2.4.4

  • Compatibility: Added support for common custom checkout field IDs such as billing_tax_number, billing_tax_office, and billing_tc_number.
  • Compatibility: Kept legacy Turkish field IDs working for existing stores and old orders.
  • Fix: Contract previews and generated PDFs now read modern and legacy tax/identity meta keys.
  • Fix: Admin missing-field warnings now translate correctly when bundled translations are newer than the installed language pack.

2.4.3

  • Admin: Checkout field availability warnings are now shown only as WordPress admin notices, not on the customer checkout page.
  • Admin: Missing checkout field notices link directly to the field mapping screen.
  • Compatibility: The warning is recorded only for users who can manage WooCommerce and is cleared when no missing fields remain.

2.4.2

  • Security: Contract PDFs are now served through protected download URLs instead of direct public uploads links.
  • Security: Added an admin PDF storage security check with Apache and Nginx server-rule guidance.
  • Security: Checkout AJAX, contract template saving, and PDF downloads now include nonce checks.
  • Security: Contract snapshots are generated server-side from order data, while legacy meta keys remain compatible.
  • Compatibility: Block checkout now sends and validates contract approval on the Store API side.
  • Compatibility: Block checkout contract approval now migrates to the default terms area before the place order button.
  • Compatibility: Classic shortcode checkout now has stronger contract field fallbacks and clearer approval validation.
  • Admin: Fields mapping screen now offers selectable checkout fields plus manual custom selectors.
  • Privacy: Removed the checkout-time external IP lookup from the block integration.
  • PDF: Restricted Dompdf remote fetching to same-site hosts by default and strengthened PDF filename generation.
  • Admin: Restricted plugin assets to plugin admin screens and fixed the email status value mismatch.
  • Release: Updated the stable tag to match the plugin version.
